body:
For you: posts you read now stay read, on each board, wherever you read them. The page is republished (now version 38). Your own use since then saved 5 kit-board marks. The `CCW` badge is fixed too (below).

## What was wrong (measured)
- **Marks were being saved.** Your read doc (`data/users/<you>/board-seen`) went from version 2242 to 2244 while I watched (02:09-02:13). So the user id, the db and the writes all worked. The orchestrator's "nothing is saved" was not right.
- **Read in the Feed, Focus or a window = never marked.** Only a post opened in its full sheet was watched. I drove the live page in Chromium as a signed-in viewer (Artifact runtime stub). The sheet wrote a mark on desktop and phone. The Feed view, the Focus view and a shift-click post window wrote none. You commented on and liked `cl12` without it ever getting a mark.
- **Two boards shared one mark per id.** Marks were keyed by the bare post id. So the kit board's `_orchestrator` comments landed in Harmonize's `_orchestrator` mark. The same goes for any id both boards have, such as the demo posts every install adds.
- Not the cause: Harmonize's own 67 open posts all had marks with matching signatures.

## The fix (`kit/board/board.template.html`, `kit/board/shim.js`, `kit/board/board_server.py`)
- **A mark per board.** An attached board's post is kept as `repos/<board>/<id>`; the primary board keeps the bare id. Old bare marks still count for the primary board. For an attached post, an old bare mark counts only if it was made on that very text, or names one of its comments. So the 15 kit posts you opened on the old page (02:13-02:22) stay read.
- **Read anywhere counts.** The body and comments in the Feed, Focus and post windows are marked by BD3's rule: half on screen for a second. Opening alone marks nothing, and nothing counts while hidden under an open post.
- **Local server:** one read doc for every board (the primary store's). An attached store's older marks show under `repos/<board>/`.

## The CCW badge that would not go away (your 02:16)
- At 02:17 the old page had marked `CCW` fully read. At 02:26 version 36 began a separate per-board mark for it that held only 1 of its 12 comments, and that partial mark hid the full one.
- Version 38 merges the two, and the later read wins, so `CCW` shows as read again. In Chromium with its real post and 13 comments: scrolling through the thread clears the badge and folds the mark into one date. A new check covers it, red on version 37 and green now.
- Comments are marked when shown: a long thread you have not scrolled through keeps its badge, by BD3's rule.

## Test first (red, then green)
`tests/test_seen_marks.py` runs `kit/claude/test_seen_marks.js` on a freshly built page:

| page | seen checks |
|---|---|
| main (built) | 6 of 9 (fails: per-board mark, Feed, window) |
| the live page before republish | 6 of 9 (the same 3) |
| version 37 | 9 of 10 (fails: the CCW case) |
| this branch / the republished page (v38) | 10 of 10 |

The checks cover: primary board read, then reload: not new; an unread post stays new (control); the same on the attached board; reading the kit board's `P-a` leaves Harmonize's identical `P-a` new; Feed; window; old marks. The local-server check fails on main (the attached board's mark landed in its own store) and passes here.

## Suites (`python3 scripts/run_all_tests.py`, after merging origin/main into the branch, as WHAT-NOT-TO-BREAK says)
7 of 7 suites pass, 0 failed. tests/ ran 91 tests, all OK, mine included. The 2 test_strings failures from before were fixed on main by CL10. `test_artifact_page.js` passes on the republished page. Nothing on the WHAT-NOT-TO-BREAK list was removed or renamed.

## In your doc after the republish (02:26-02:30, your own use)
`repos/board/cl11-...`, `repos/board/cl9-...`, `repos/board/cl13-...`, `repos/board/CCW-...` and `repos/board/_orchestrator`. The last is now separate from Harmonize's `_orchestrator`. The doc went from 200 to 204 marks, version 2323.

## Not done {fold}
- **Harmonize repo:** this session was refused access to `anlonlt/harmonize` (add_repo denied). So no `install.py --update` and no Harmonize push. The page was republished from the live page plus exactly this diff (the live page had no other change). Harmonize's next `install.py --update` from the kit brings the same code.
- **Kit main:** I pushed branch `cl21-seen-state` only, with origin/main already merged in (7817842); trunk push is off. The merge into main is for the orchestrator. It touches only the seen code and its tests, plus 3 tokens in strings.py.
- **The live page** is version 36's base (from before CL10) plus only the CL21 changes. CL10's page changes reach it with Harmonize's next `install.py --update` and republish (WHAT-NOT-TO-BREAK § 5).

## Commits {fold}
`2a6a474` per-board marks, read anywhere, one local seen doc, tests. `3dff29d` old kit marks on the same text honoured. `20bce72`: a partial mark no longer hides the full read (CCW). `7817842` merge of origin/main.
